items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Zygomatic bone.
o: the plate that forms the prominence of the cheek
a joint in which the surfaces are joined by cartilage and only slight movement occurs
the lateral bone of the forearm, lying on the thumb side
the flat breastbone in the midline of the front of the chest
items.s: Zygomatic bone: the plate that forms the prominence of the cheek. The other options describe Sternum, Radius, Cartilaginous union.

items.q: Which term is described by “one of the five large bones of the lower back”?
o: Spine
Atlas
Sacrum
Lumbar vertebra
items.s: Lumbar vertebra is one of the five large bones of the lower back.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Foramen?
o: a freely movable union in which a rounded head sits in a cup-shaped cavity, as at the shoulder
the vertical cut that separates the front of the body from the back
an opening in a bone through which vessels or nerves pass
the plate at the back and base of the skull, pierced by the opening for the spinal cord
items.s: Foramen: an opening in a bone through which vessels or nerves pass. The other options describe Ball and socket joint, Coronal plane, Occipital bone.

items.q: The statement “the small bone in front of the knee developed within the tendon of the quadriceps” describes which of the following?
o: Tibia
Patella
Fibula
Femur
items.s: Patella is the small bone in front of the knee developed within the tendon of the quadriceps.

items.q: Which term is described by “a joint in which the surfaces are joined by cartilage and only slight movement occurs”?
o: Cartilaginous union
Hinge joint
Synovial membrane
Bursa
items.s: Cartilaginous union is a joint in which the surfaces are joined by cartilage and only slight movement occurs.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Temporal bone.
o: the plate at the side of the skull that houses the organs of hearing
straightening at a joint so that the angle between the two parts increases
a union in which a rounded part turns within a ring, as between the first two neck vertebrae
the lower jaw, the only freely movable bone of the skull
items.s: Temporal bone: the plate at the side of the skull that houses the organs of hearing. The other options describe Extension, Mandible, Pivot joint.

items.q: Cervical vertebra may be defined as
o: one of the seven bones of the neck region, the first two of which are atypical
one of the twelve bones of the trunk that articulate with ribs
a union in which a rounded part turns within a ring, as between the first two neck vertebrae
the flat breastbone in the midline of the front of the chest
items.s: Cervical vertebra: one of the seven bones of the neck region, the first two of which are atypical. The other options describe Pivot joint, Thoracic vertebra, Sternum.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Median plane?
o: the vertical division through the midline that gives equal right and left halves
the bones of the limbs together with the girdles that attach them
any vertical cut parallel to the midline that gives unequal right and left parts
the region between the diaphragm above and the pelvis below, containing the viscera
items.s: Median plane: the vertical division through the midline that gives equal right and left halves. The other options describe Appendicular skeleton, Abdomen, Parasagittal plane.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Anatomic posture?
o: a muscle that assists another and steadies the part during movement
the reference stance of standing erect with the face forward and the palms turned forward
the two-headed muscle at the front of the arm that flexes the elbow
the plate that forms the prominence of the cheek
items.s: Anatomic posture: the reference stance of standing erect with the face forward and the palms turned forward. The other options describe Synergist, Zygomatic bone, Biceps brachii.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Insertion of a muscle?
o: the attachment that is drawn towards the fixed point when contraction occurs
farther from the midline, towards the side of the body
the two-headed muscle at the front of the arm that flexes the elbow
one of the five large bones of the lower back
items.s: Insertion of a muscle: the attachment that is drawn towards the fixed point when contraction occurs. The other options describe Lumbar vertebra, Lateral, Biceps brachii.

items.q: Medullary cavity may be defined as
o: the central space of a long bone that holds marrow
the attachment that is drawn towards the fixed point when contraction occurs
straightening at a joint so that the angle between the two parts increases
farther from the midline, towards the side of the body
items.s: Medullary cavity: the central space of a long bone that holds marrow. The other options describe Insertion of a muscle, Lateral, Extension.

items.q: Which term is described by “a broad rounded elevation on a bone that gives attachment to muscle”?
o: Metaphysis
Tuberosity
Sesamoid ossicle
Diaphysis
items.s: Tuberosity is a broad rounded elevation on a bone that gives attachment to muscle.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Medullary cavity?
o: the small bone in front of the knee developed within the tendon of the quadriceps
a freely movable union in which a lubricated space lies between the apposed surfaces
the muscle that opposes and controls the action of another muscle
the central space of a long bone that holds marrow
items.s: Medullary cavity: the central space of a long bone that holds marrow. The other options describe Antagonist, Synovial joint, Patella.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Epiphysis?
o: a union whose two surfaces are reciprocally hollow and rounded, as at the base of the thumb
the first neck vertebra, which supports the skull and allows nodding
a small nodule developed within a tendon where it crosses a joint, as at the knee
the expanded end of a long bone that carries the articular surface
items.s: Epiphysis: the expanded end of a long bone that carries the articular surface. The other options describe Saddle joint, Sesamoid ossicle, Atlas.

items.q: Which term is described by “the lining of a joint cavity that secretes the fluid which lubricates it”?
o: Hinge joint
Synovial membrane
Cartilaginous union
Ligament
items.s: Synovial membrane is the lining of a joint cavity that secretes the fluid which lubricates it.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Origin of a muscle?
o: the attachment that stays relatively fixed when contraction occurs
the flat triangular bone at the back of the shoulder
the eight small bones of the wrist arranged in two rows
the network of nerves in the armpit that supplies the whole upper limb
items.s: Origin of a muscle: the attachment that stays relatively fixed when contraction occurs. The other options describe Carpals, Scapula, Brachial plexus.

items.q: The statement “the band running from the front of the hip bone to the pubic region” describes which of the following?
o: Cubital fossa
Inguinal ligament
Popliteal fossa
Abdomen
items.s: Inguinal ligament is the band running from the front of the hip bone to the pubic region.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Brachial plexus?
o: the network of nerves in the armpit that supplies the whole upper limb
the large bone of the leg whose upper surface bears body weight
the pad of fibrocartilage between the bodies of adjacent vertebrae
the central space of a long bone that holds marrow
items.s: Brachial plexus: the network of nerves in the armpit that supplies the whole upper limb. The other options describe Intervertebral disc, Tibia, Medullary cavity.

items.q: Zygomatic bone may be defined as
o: the series of bones from skull to pelvis that encloses the spinal cord
the plate at the side of the skull that houses the organs of hearing
the plate that forms the prominence of the cheek
a small nodule developed within a tendon where it crosses a joint, as at the knee
items.s: Zygomatic bone: the plate that forms the prominence of the cheek. The other options describe Temporal bone, Spine, Sesamoid ossicle.

items.q: Which term is described by “the large opening at the base of the skull through which the spinal cord passes”?
o: Occipital bone
Foramen magnum
Temporal bone
Parietal bone
items.s: Foramen magnum is the large opening at the base of the skull through which the spinal cord passes.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Maxilla?
o: the four-headed muscle at the front of the thigh that straightens the knee
the upper jaw bone that carries the upper teeth and forms part of the eye socket
the tubular shaft of a long bone
the collar bone that connects the breastbone to the shoulder blade
items.s: Maxilla: the upper jaw bone that carries the upper teeth and forms part of the eye socket. The other options describe Diaphysis, Clavicle, Quadriceps femoris.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Growth plate.
o: the layer of cartilage near the end of a growing bone where length is added
a broad rounded elevation on a bone that gives attachment to muscle
a muscle that assists another and steadies the part during movement
a joint in which the surfaces are tied by dense connective tissue and hardly move
items.s: Growth plate: the layer of cartilage near the end of a growing bone where length is added. The other options describe Tuberosity, Synergist, Fibrous union.

items.q: Which term is described by “the thick muscle forming the rounded contour of the shoulder”?
o: Scapula
Ulna
Biceps brachii
Deltoid
items.s: Deltoid is the thick muscle forming the rounded contour of the shoulder.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Fibrous union.
o: the eight small bones of the wrist arranged in two rows
a joint in which the surfaces are tied by dense connective tissue and hardly move
the vertical cut that separates the front of the body from the back
the flat breastbone in the midline of the front of the chest
items.s: Fibrous union: a joint in which the surfaces are tied by dense connective tissue and hardly move. The other options describe Carpals, Coronal plane, Sternum.

items.q: Flexion may be defined as
o: the long bone of the arm between shoulder and elbow
the first neck vertebra, which supports the skull and allows nodding
the thick muscle forming the rounded contour of the shoulder
bending at a joint so that the angle between the two parts decreases
items.s: Flexion: bending at a joint so that the angle between the two parts decreases. The other options describe Humerus, Deltoid, Atlas.

items.q: The statement “the attachment that is drawn towards the fixed point when contraction occurs” describes which of the following?
o: Prime mover
Antagonist
Insertion of a muscle
Extension
items.s: Insertion of a muscle is the attachment that is drawn towards the fixed point when contraction occurs.

items.q: The statement “the lining of a joint cavity that secretes the fluid which lubricates it” describes which of the following?
o: Ball and socket joint
Ligament
Hinge joint
Synovial membrane
items.s: Synovial membrane is the lining of a joint cavity that secretes the fluid which lubricates it.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Rib?
o: one of the seven bones of the neck region, the first two of which are atypical
a band of fibrous tissue joining one bone to another across a joint
any vertical cut parallel to the midline that gives unequal right and left parts
a curved flat bone arching from a thoracic vertebra towards the front of the chest
items.s: Rib: a curved flat bone arching from a thoracic vertebra towards the front of the chest. The other options describe Ligament, Parasagittal plane, Cervical vertebra.

items.q: Adduction may be defined as
o: the finger bones, three in each finger and two in the thumb
the vertical cut that separates the front of the body from the back
movement of a part towards the midline of the body
the region between the diaphragm above and the pelvis below, containing the viscera
items.s: Adduction: movement of a part towards the midline of the body. The other options describe Abdomen, Coronal plane, Phalanges of the hand.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Carpals.
o: the two-headed calf muscle that points the foot downwards at the ankle
striated voluntary tissue that produces movement of the skeleton when it contracts
the eight small bones of the wrist arranged in two rows
the attachment that is drawn towards the fixed point when contraction occurs
items.s: Carpals: the eight small bones of the wrist arranged in two rows. The other options describe Gastrocnemius, Skeletal muscle, Insertion of a muscle.

items.q: Which term is described by “the expanded end of a long bone that carries the articular surface”?
o: Growth plate
Epiphysis
Foramen
Condyle
items.s: Epiphysis is the expanded end of a long bone that carries the articular surface.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Sesamoid ossicle.
o: the plate that forms the prominence of the cheek
a small nodule developed within a tendon where it crosses a joint, as at the knee
the lower jaw, the only freely movable bone of the skull
the upper jaw bone that carries the upper teeth and forms part of the eye socket
items.s: Sesamoid ossicle: a small nodule developed within a tendon where it crosses a joint, as at the knee. The other options describe Maxilla, Mandible, Zygomatic bone.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Biceps brachii.
o: the vertical division through the midline that gives equal right and left halves
the two-headed muscle at the front of the arm that flexes the elbow
the plate at the back and base of the skull, pierced by the opening for the spinal cord
the plate at the side of the skull that houses the organs of hearing
items.s: Biceps brachii: the two-headed muscle at the front of the arm that flexes the elbow. The other options describe Median plane, Temporal bone, Occipital bone.

items.q: All of the following belong to Upper limb EXCEPT
o: Sternum
Clavicle
Scapula
Humerus
items.s: Every other option belongs to Upper limb. “Sternum” belongs to Vertebral column and thoracic cage, not Upper limb.

items.q: Which term is described by “a small fluid-filled sac between a tendon and bone that reduces friction”?
o: Hinge joint
Synovial membrane
Bursa
Ball and socket joint
items.s: Bursa is a small fluid-filled sac between a tendon and bone that reduces friction.

items.q: The statement “the first neck vertebra, which supports the skull and allows nodding” describes which of the following?
o: Lumbar vertebra
Thoracic vertebra
Sternum
Atlas
items.s: Atlas is the first neck vertebra, which supports the skull and allows nodding.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Intervertebral disc?
o: farther along a limb from the trunk
a joint in which the surfaces are tied by dense connective tissue and hardly move
the pad of fibrocartilage between the bodies of adjacent vertebrae
the thick muscle forming the rounded contour of the shoulder
items.s: Intervertebral disc: the pad of fibrocartilage between the bodies of adjacent vertebrae. The other options describe Fibrous union, Distal, Deltoid.

items.q: Which term is described by “the long bone of the thigh, the longest and heaviest in the body”?
o: Quadriceps femoris
Tibia
Calcaneus
Femur
items.s: Femur is the long bone of the thigh, the longest and heaviest in the body.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Tibia?
o: the muscle chiefly responsible for producing a particular movement
the large bone of the leg whose upper surface bears body weight
the flat triangular bone at the back of the shoulder
the reference stance of standing erect with the face forward and the palms turned forward
items.s: Tibia: the large bone of the leg whose upper surface bears body weight. The other options describe Anatomic posture, Prime mover, Scapula.

items.q: The statement “a muscle that assists another and steadies the part during movement” describes which of the following?
o: Origin of a muscle
Extension
Antagonist
Synergist
items.s: Synergist is a muscle that assists another and steadies the part during movement.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Spine.
o: movement of a part towards the midline of the body
one of the pair of flat plates forming the side wall and roof of the skull
a freely movable union in which a rounded head sits in a cup-shaped cavity, as at the shoulder
the series of bones from skull to pelvis that encloses the spinal cord
items.s: Spine: the series of bones from skull to pelvis that encloses the spinal cord. The other options describe Parietal bone, Adduction, Ball and socket joint.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Deltoid?
o: the thick muscle forming the rounded contour of the shoulder
the diamond-shaped hollow at the back of the knee
the collar bone that connects the breastbone to the shoulder blade
the small bone in front of the knee developed within the tendon of the quadriceps
items.s: Deltoid: the thick muscle forming the rounded contour of the shoulder. The other options describe Popliteal fossa, Patella, Clavicle.

items.q: Mandible may be defined as
o: the large opening at the base of the skull through which the spinal cord passes
the lower jaw, the only freely movable bone of the skull
the attachment that stays relatively fixed when contraction occurs
a freely movable union in which a lubricated space lies between the apposed surfaces
items.s: Mandible: the lower jaw, the only freely movable bone of the skull. The other options describe Origin of a muscle, Synovial joint, Foramen magnum.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Inguinal ligament.
o: striated voluntary tissue that produces movement of the skeleton when it contracts
the collar bone that connects the breastbone to the shoulder blade
the band running from the front of the hip bone to the pubic region
the fused mass of vertebrae that forms the back wall of the pelvis
items.s: Inguinal ligament: the band running from the front of the hip bone to the pubic region. The other options describe Skeletal muscle, Sacrum, Clavicle.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Lumbar vertebra?
o: the first neck vertebra, which supports the skull and allows nodding
the fused mass of vertebrae that forms the back wall of the pelvis
one of the five large bones of the lower back
a small nodule developed within a tendon where it crosses a joint, as at the knee
items.s: Lumbar vertebra: one of the five large bones of the lower back. The other options describe Sacrum, Atlas, Sesamoid ossicle.

items.q: Quadriceps femoris may be defined as
o: the plate at the side of the skull that houses the organs of hearing
the four-headed muscle at the front of the thigh that straightens the knee
movement of a part away from the midline of the body
farther from the midline, towards the side of the body
items.s: Quadriceps femoris: the four-headed muscle at the front of the thigh that straightens the knee. The other options describe Lateral, Abduction, Temporal bone.

items.q: The statement “the long bone of the arm between shoulder and elbow” describes which of the following?
o: Deltoid
Ulna
Humerus
Carpals
items.s: Humerus is the long bone of the arm between shoulder and elbow.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Humerus.
o: the large opening at the base of the skull through which the spinal cord passes
the layer of cartilage near the end of a growing bone where length is added
the long bone of the arm between shoulder and elbow
the lateral bone of the forearm, lying on the thumb side
items.s: Humerus: the long bone of the arm between shoulder and elbow. The other options describe Radius, Foramen magnum, Growth plate.

items.q: Which term is described by “a rounded articular projection at the end of a bone”?
o: Medullary cavity
Sesamoid ossicle
Condyle
Foramen
items.s: Condyle is a rounded articular projection at the end of a bone.

items.q: Which term is described by “the flat triangular bone at the back of the shoulder”?
o: Radius
Biceps brachii
Scapula
Clavicle
items.s: Scapula is the flat triangular bone at the back of the shoulder.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Thorax?
o: any vertical cut parallel to the midline that gives unequal right and left parts
the medial bone of the forearm that forms the point of the elbow
a freely movable union in which a rounded head sits in a cup-shaped cavity, as at the shoulder
the region enclosed by the ribs, breastbone and thoracic vertebrae
items.s: Thorax: the region enclosed by the ribs, breastbone and thoracic vertebrae. The other options describe Ball and socket joint, Parasagittal plane, Ulna.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Os coxae?
o: the large opening at the base of the skull through which the spinal cord passes
the large irregular bone formed by fusion of the ilium, ischium and pubis
a broad rounded elevation on a bone that gives attachment to muscle
a freely movable union in which a rounded head sits in a cup-shaped cavity, as at the shoulder
items.s: Os coxae: the large irregular bone formed by fusion of the ilium, ischium and pubis. The other options describe Foramen magnum, Ball and socket joint, Tuberosity.

items.q: The statement “straightening at a joint so that the angle between the two parts increases” describes which of the following?
o: Abduction
Flexion
Prime mover
Extension
items.s: Extension is straightening at a joint so that the angle between the two parts increases.

items.q: Which term is described by “a freely movable union in which a lubricated space lies between the apposed surfaces”?
o: Synovial joint
Fibrous union
Saddle joint
Pivot joint
items.s: Synovial joint is a freely movable union in which a lubricated space lies between the apposed surfaces.

items.q: Which term is described by “the muscle chiefly responsible for producing a particular movement”?
o: Insertion of a muscle
Flexion
Prime mover
Skeletal muscle
items.s: Prime mover is the muscle chiefly responsible for producing a particular movement.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Femur?
o: a joint in which the surfaces are tied by dense connective tissue and hardly move
the long bone of the thigh, the longest and heaviest in the body
the small bone in front of the knee developed within the tendon of the quadriceps
the lining of a joint cavity that secretes the fluid which lubricates it
items.s: Femur: the long bone of the thigh, the longest and heaviest in the body. The other options describe Patella, Fibrous union, Synovial membrane.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Frontal bone?
o: the attachment that stays relatively fixed when contraction occurs
the medial bone of the forearm that forms the point of the elbow
the plate at the back and base of the skull, pierced by the opening for the spinal cord
the flat plate forming the forehead and the roof of each eye socket
items.s: Frontal bone: the flat plate forming the forehead and the roof of each eye socket. The other options describe Ulna, Occipital bone, Origin of a muscle.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Cubital fossa?
o: the triangular hollow at the front of the elbow
nearer to the trunk or to the point where a limb is attached
the plate that forms the prominence of the cheek
an opening in a bone through which vessels or nerves pass
items.s: Cubital fossa: the triangular hollow at the front of the elbow. The other options describe Foramen, Proximal, Zygomatic bone.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Insertion of a muscle?
o: a broad rounded elevation on a bone that gives attachment to muscle
the attachment that is drawn towards the fixed point when contraction occurs
a curved flat bone arching from a thoracic vertebra towards the front of the chest
one of the twelve bones of the trunk that articulate with ribs
items.s: Insertion of a muscle: the attachment that is drawn towards the fixed point when contraction occurs. The other options describe Tuberosity, Thoracic vertebra, Rib.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Condyle.
o: an opening in a bone through which vessels or nerves pass
the reference stance of standing erect with the face forward and the palms turned forward
one of the seven bones of the neck region, the first two of which are atypical
a rounded articular projection at the end of a bone
items.s: Condyle: a rounded articular projection at the end of a bone. The other options describe Cervical vertebra, Anatomic posture, Foramen.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Appendicular skeleton?
o: the second neck vertebra, whose upward peg forms the pivot for turning the head
the bones of the limbs together with the girdles that attach them
the slender bone on the lateral side of the leg that carries no weight
the largest bone of the foot, forming the heel
items.s: Appendicular skeleton: the bones of the limbs together with the girdles that attach them. The other options describe Fibula, Calcaneus, Axis.

items.q: Distal may be defined as
o: a rounded articular projection at the end of a bone
farther along a limb from the trunk
the expanded end of a long bone that carries the articular surface
a muscle that assists another and steadies the part during movement
items.s: Distal: farther along a limb from the trunk. The other options describe Condyle, Epiphysis, Synergist.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Medial?
o: the plate at the back and base of the skull, pierced by the opening for the spinal cord
nearer to the midline of the body
the lining of a joint cavity that secretes the fluid which lubricates it
farther from the midline, towards the side of the body
items.s: Medial: nearer to the midline of the body. The other options describe Occipital bone, Lateral, Synovial membrane.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Antagonist?
o: striated voluntary tissue that produces movement of the skeleton when it contracts
the muscle that opposes and controls the action of another muscle
a band of fibrous tissue joining one bone to another across a joint
the band running from the front of the hip bone to the pubic region
items.s: Antagonist: the muscle that opposes and controls the action of another muscle. The other options describe Inguinal ligament, Skeletal muscle, Ligament.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Tarsals?
o: the region enclosed by the ribs, breastbone and thoracic vertebrae
striated voluntary tissue that produces movement of the skeleton when it contracts
the seven bones forming the heel and the back part of the foot
the two-headed calf muscle that points the foot downwards at the ankle
items.s: Tarsals: the seven bones forming the heel and the back part of the foot. The other options describe Skeletal muscle, Gastrocnemius, Thorax.

items.q: The statement “the region where the shaft of a long bone meets its expanded end” describes which of the following?
o: Metaphysis
Medullary cavity
Foramen
Periosteum
items.s: Metaphysis is the region where the shaft of a long bone meets its expanded end.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Ligament?
o: the region where the shaft of a long bone meets its expanded end
a band of fibrous tissue joining one bone to another across a joint
the layer of cartilage near the end of a growing bone where length is added
movement of a part away from the midline of the body
items.s: Ligament: a band of fibrous tissue joining one bone to another across a joint. The other options describe Metaphysis, Abduction, Growth plate.

items.q: Spine may be defined as
o: the region where the shaft of a long bone meets its expanded end
the first neck vertebra, which supports the skull and allows nodding
the upper jaw bone that carries the upper teeth and forms part of the eye socket
the series of bones from skull to pelvis that encloses the spinal cord
items.s: Spine: the series of bones from skull to pelvis that encloses the spinal cord. The other options describe Atlas, Maxilla, Metaphysis.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Axial skeleton.
o: farther from the midline, towards the side of the body
the skull, spinal column, ribs and breastbone, which form the central framework
the tubular shaft of a long bone
the large irregular bone formed by fusion of the ilium, ischium and pubis
items.s: Axial skeleton: the skull, spinal column, ribs and breastbone, which form the central framework. The other options describe Diaphysis, Lateral, Os coxae.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Coronal plane?
o: the tubular shaft of a long bone
the vertical cut that separates the front of the body from the back
a rounded articular projection at the end of a bone
a muscle that assists another and steadies the part during movement
items.s: Coronal plane: the vertical cut that separates the front of the body from the back. The other options describe Synergist, Condyle, Diaphysis.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Proximal?
o: nearer to the trunk or to the point where a limb is attached
the flat plate forming the forehead and the roof of each eye socket
the eight small bones of the wrist arranged in two rows
a band of fibrous tissue joining one bone to another across a joint
items.s: Proximal: nearer to the trunk or to the point where a limb is attached. The other options describe Ligament, Carpals, Frontal bone.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Popliteal fossa.
o: the finger bones, three in each finger and two in the thumb
the two-headed calf muscle that points the foot downwards at the ankle
the band running from the front of the hip bone to the pubic region
the diamond-shaped hollow at the back of the knee
items.s: Popliteal fossa: the diamond-shaped hollow at the back of the knee. The other options describe Inguinal ligament, Gastrocnemius, Phalanges of the hand.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Sesamoid ossicle?
o: the two-headed muscle at the front of the arm that flexes the elbow
a union that permits movement in one plane only, as at the elbow
the muscle that opposes and controls the action of another muscle
a small nodule developed within a tendon where it crosses a joint, as at the knee
items.s: Sesamoid ossicle: a small nodule developed within a tendon where it crosses a joint, as at the knee. The other options describe Antagonist, Biceps brachii, Hinge joint.

items.q: Synergist may be defined as
o: a muscle that assists another and steadies the part during movement
the collar bone that connects the breastbone to the shoulder blade
a band of fibrous tissue joining one bone to another across a joint
the flat plate forming the forehead and the roof of each eye socket
items.s: Synergist: a muscle that assists another and steadies the part during movement. The other options describe Ligament, Frontal bone, Clavicle.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Pivot joint?
o: the part of the skull that encloses and protects the brain
a union in which a rounded part turns within a ring, as between the first two neck vertebrae
movement of a part towards the midline of the body
one of the five large bones of the lower back
items.s: Pivot joint: a union in which a rounded part turns within a ring, as between the first two neck vertebrae. The other options describe Adduction, Cranium, Lumbar vertebra.

items.q: Axis is best described as
o: the pad of fibrocartilage between the bodies of adjacent vertebrae
a curved flat bone arching from a thoracic vertebra towards the front of the chest
one of the twelve bones of the trunk that articulate with ribs
the second neck vertebra, whose upward peg forms the pivot for turning the head
items.s: Axis: the second neck vertebra, whose upward peg forms the pivot for turning the head. The other options describe Thoracic vertebra, Rib, Intervertebral disc.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what Clavicle means.
o: the collar bone that connects the breastbone to the shoulder blade
the finger bones, three in each finger and two in the thumb
the lateral bone of the forearm, lying on the thumb side
the medial bone of the forearm that forms the point of the elbow
items.s: Clavicle: the collar bone that connects the breastbone to the shoulder blade. The other options describe Radius, Ulna, Phalanges of the hand.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what Synovial joint means.
o: a union that permits movement in one plane only, as at the elbow

striated voluntary tissue that produces movement of the skeleton when it contracts
the muscle chiefly responsible for producing a particular movement
the muscle that opposes and controls the action of another muscle
items.s: Prime mover: the muscle chiefly responsible for producing a particular movement. The other options describe Extension, Skeletal muscle, Antagonist.

items.q: “the collar bone that connects the breastbone to the shoulder blade” is the definition of
o: Carpals
Radius
Clavicle
Humerus
items.s: Clavicle is the collar bone that connects the breastbone to the shoulder blade.

items.q: The correct meaning of Hinge joint is
o: the lining of a joint cavity that secretes the fluid which lubricates it
a union that permits movement in one plane only, as at the elbow
a freely movable union in which a rounded head sits in a cup-shaped cavity, as at the shoulder
a band of fibrous tissue joining one bone to another across a joint
items.s: Hinge joint: a union that permits movement in one plane only, as at the elbow. The other options describe Synovial membrane, Ball and socket joint, Ligament.

items.q: “the band running from the front of the hip bone to the pubic region” is the definition of
o: Appendicular skeleton
Cubital fossa
Inguinal ligament
Axial skeleton
items.s: Inguinal ligament is the band running from the front of the hip bone to the pubic region.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Synovial joint.
o: a union that permits movement in one plane only, as at the elbow
a joint in which the surfaces are tied by dense connective tissue and hardly move
a freely movable union in which a lubricated space lies between the apposed surfaces
a freely movable union in which a rounded head sits in a cup-shaped cavity, as at the shoulder
items.s: Synovial joint: a freely movable union in which a lubricated space lies between the apposed surfaces. The other options describe Hinge joint, Fibrous union, Ball and socket joint.

items.q: In this course, Condyle refers to
o: a rounded articular projection at the end of a bone
a small nodule developed within a tendon where it crosses a joint, as at the knee
the expanded end of a long bone that carries the articular surface
the layer of cartilage near the end of a growing bone where length is added
items.s: Condyle: a rounded articular projection at the end of a bone. The other options describe Epiphysis, Growth plate, Sesamoid ossicle.

items.q: The correct meaning of Radius is
o: the thick muscle forming the rounded contour of the shoulder
the flat triangular bone at the back of the shoulder
the lateral bone of the forearm, lying on the thumb side
the finger bones, three in each finger and two in the thumb
items.s: Radius: the lateral bone of the forearm, lying on the thumb side. The other options describe Deltoid, Scapula, Phalanges of the hand.

items.q: The correct meaning of Fibrous union is
o: a small fluid-filled sac between a tendon and bone that reduces friction
a freely movable union in which a lubricated space lies between the apposed surfaces
a band of fibrous tissue joining one bone to another across a joint
a joint in which the surfaces are tied by dense connective tissue and hardly move
items.s: Fibrous union: a joint in which the surfaces are tied by dense connective tissue and hardly move. The other options describe Bursa, Synovial joint, Ligament.

items.q: The correct meaning of Deltoid is
o: the two-headed muscle at the front of the arm that flexes the elbow
the long bone of the arm between shoulder and elbow
the lateral bone of the forearm, lying on the thumb side
the thick muscle forming the rounded contour of the shoulder
items.s: Deltoid: the thick muscle forming the rounded contour of the shoulder. The other options describe Humerus, Radius, Biceps brachii.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a joint in which the surfaces are tied by dense connective tissue and hardly move”
o: Saddle joint
Fibrous union
Pivot joint
Ball and socket joint
items.s: Fibrous union is a joint in which the surfaces are tied by dense connective tissue and hardly move.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Parasagittal plane?

the vertical division through the midline that gives equal right and left halves
any vertical cut parallel to the midline that gives unequal right and left parts
a horizontal cut lying at right angles to the long axis of the body
items.s: Parasagittal plane: any vertical cut parallel to the midline that gives unequal right and left parts. The other options describe Transverse plane, Anatomic posture, Median plane.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Medullary cavity?
o: the expanded end of a long bone that carries the articular surface
a rounded articular projection at the end of a bone
the layer of cartilage near the end of a growing bone where length is added
the central space of a long bone that holds marrow
items.s: Medullary cavity: the central space of a long bone that holds marrow. The other options describe Condyle, Epiphysis, Growth plate.

items.q: “the flat triangular bone at the back of the shoulder” is the definition of
o: Deltoid
Scapula
Ulna
Clavicle
items.s: Scapula is the flat triangular bone at the back of the shoulder.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Condyle?
o: a rounded articular projection at the end of a bone
the tubular shaft of a long bone
the fibrous membrane covering the outer surface of a bone except where cartilage caps it
a broad rounded elevation on a bone that gives attachment to muscle
items.s: Condyle: a rounded articular projection at the end of a bone. The other options describe Periosteum, Diaphysis, Tuberosity.

items.q: The correct meaning of Thoracic vertebra is
o: the fused mass of vertebrae that forms the back wall of the pelvis
the second neck vertebra, whose upward peg forms the pivot for turning the head
one of the seven bones of the neck region, the first two of which are atypical
one of the twelve bones of the trunk that articulate with ribs
items.s: Thoracic vertebra: one of the twelve bones of the trunk that articulate with ribs. The other options describe Axis, Sacrum, Cervical vertebra.

items.q: “a union whose two surfaces are reciprocally hollow and rounded, as at the base of the thumb” is the definition of
o: Fibrous union
Cartilaginous union
Hinge joint
Saddle joint
items.s: Saddle joint is a union whose two surfaces are reciprocally hollow and rounded, as at the base of the thumb.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “one of the pair of flat plates forming the side wall and roof of the skull”
o: Cranium
Parietal bone
Temporal bone
Mandible
items.s: Parietal bone is one of the pair of flat plates forming the side wall and roof of the skull.

items.q: Transverse plane may be defined as

a slanted cut that is neither vertical nor horizontal
a horizontal cut lying at right angles to the long axis of the body
any vertical cut parallel to the midline that gives unequal right and left parts

items.q: Thorax may be defined as

the bones of the limbs together with the girdles that attach them
the skull, spinal column, ribs and breastbone, which form the central framework
the region between the diaphragm above and the pelvis below, containing the viscera
items.s: Thorax: the region enclosed by the ribs, breastbone and thoracic vertebrae. The other options describe Abdomen, Appendicular skeleton, Axial skeleton.

items.q: “the first neck vertebra, which supports the skull and allows nodding” is the definition of
o: Lumbar vertebra
Rib
Atlas
Cervical vertebra
items.s: Atlas is the first neck vertebra, which supports the skull and allows nodding.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Ulna.
o: the finger bones, three in each finger and two in the thumb
the medial bone of the forearm that forms the point of the elbow
the collar bone that connects the breastbone to the shoulder blade
the long bone of the arm between shoulder and elbow

items.q: In this course, Sternum refers to
o: one of the seven bones of the neck region, the first two of which are atypical
one of the twelve bones of the trunk that articulate with ribs
the flat breastbone in the midline of the front of the chest
the pad of fibrocartilage between the bodies of adjacent vertebrae

items.q: Foramen magnum may be defined as

the large opening at the base of the skull through which the spinal cord passes
the plate that forms the prominence of the cheek
items.s: Foramen magnum: the large opening at the base of the skull through which the spinal cord passes. The other options describe Maxilla, Occipital bone, Zygomatic bone.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the attachment that is drawn towards the fixed point when contraction occurs”
o: Insertion of a muscle
Extension
Origin of a muscle
Synergist

items.q: “a slanted cut that is neither vertical nor horizontal” is the definition of
o: Parasagittal plane
Anatomic posture
Oblique plane
Coronal plane
items.s: Oblique plane is a slanted cut that is neither vertical nor horizontal.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the long bone of the thigh, the longest and heaviest in the body”

Femur
Fibula
Quadriceps femoris

a horizontal cut lying at right angles to the long axis of the body
nearer to the midline of the body
farther from the midline, towards the side of the body

items.q: “any vertical cut parallel to the midline that gives unequal right and left parts” is the definition of
o: Parasagittal plane
Transverse plane
Coronal plane
Anatomic posture

items.q: The correct meaning of Temporal bone is

the plate at the back and base of the skull, pierced by the opening for the spinal cord
the plate at the side of the skull that houses the organs of hearing
the upper jaw bone that carries the upper teeth and forms part of the eye socket

items.q: “a horizontal cut lying at right angles to the long axis of the body” is the definition of
o: Medial
Oblique plane
Proximal

movement of a part towards the midline of the body
movement of a part away from the midline of the body

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Axial skeleton.
o: the region enclosed by the ribs, breastbone and thoracic vertebrae
the bones of the limbs together with the girdles that attach them
the region between the diaphragm above and the pelvis below, containing the viscera
the skull, spinal column, ribs and breastbone, which form the central framework

items.q: “the largest bone of the foot, forming the heel” is the definition of

Calcaneus
Tibia
Fibula

an opening in a bone through which vessels or nerves pass
a broad rounded elevation on a bone that gives attachment to muscle
the central space of a long bone that holds marrow

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Ball and socket joint?
o: a band of fibrous tissue joining one bone to another across a joint
a union in which a rounded part turns within a ring, as between the first two neck vertebrae
a joint in which the surfaces are tied by dense connective tissue and hardly move
a freely movable union in which a rounded head sits in a cup-shaped cavity, as at the shoulder

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “farther from the midline, towards the side of the body”
o: Lateral
Distal
Oblique plane
Coronal plane

o: Abdomen
Axial skeleton
Cubital fossa
Popliteal fossa

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Sternum.

the second neck vertebra, whose upward peg forms the pivot for turning the head
the fused mass of vertebrae that forms the back wall of the pelvis
the flat breastbone in the midline of the front of the chest
items.s: Sternum: the flat breastbone in the midline of the front of the chest. The other options describe Rib, Axis, Sacrum.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Calcaneus?
o: the four-headed muscle at the front of the thigh that straightens the knee
the seven bones forming the heel and the back part of the foot
the small bone in front of the knee developed within the tendon of the quadriceps
the largest bone of the foot, forming the heel

items.q: Synovial joint may be defined as

the lining of a joint cavity that secretes the fluid which lubricates it

bending at a joint so that the angle between the two parts decreases
movement of a part away from the midline of the body
the muscle chiefly responsible for producing a particular movement

Foramen

the part of the skull that encloses and protects the brain

the long bone of the arm between shoulder and elbow
the eight small bones of the wrist arranged in two rows

a horizontal cut lying at right angles to the long axis of the body
the reference stance of standing erect with the face forward and the palms turned forward

the triangular hollow at the front of the elbow
the region between the diaphragm above and the pelvis below, containing the viscera

Tuberosity
Diaphysis
Medullary cavity

the region enclosed by the ribs, breastbone and thoracic vertebrae
the region between the diaphragm above and the pelvis below, containing the viscera
the band running from the front of the hip bone to the pubic region

the lining of a joint cavity that secretes the fluid which lubricates it
